requirement: R13 wave 2: one read route ported end to end

route.hostCorrelation: Present in the host route table per S26c; requiresHostEndpoint=false. No host change.

clientContract.request: GET /api/role-model/operator/observability-snapshot; accept: application/json; cache:no-store; Authorization: Bearer <token> only when a token is provisioned; the caller AbortSignal is forwarded.
clientContract.response: 200 JSON {schemaVersion, metrics}; rows sorted by name; empty metrics -> empty; non-200 -> error using observabilityErrorMessage(status, reason); invalid metrics -> 'Observability read failed: invalid response'.
clientContract.injection: ShellOptions.readObservability (ObservabilityReader); default createObservabilityClient() with the real fetch. Tests inject fetch and assert URL, headers, token absence/presence and signal identity.

states.success: data-observability-state=ok; metric rows with name/count/incremental; document title Observability | RM3 Foldkit shell.
states.loading: data-observability-state=loading; aria-busy; 'Loading observability snapshot…'; resolves to empty.
states.error: data-observability-state=error; role=alert; exact phrase 'Observability read failed: HTTP 503 (unavailable)'.

refresh: The page does not create an owner. A contiguous RuntimeRevisionReceived on the route dispatches ReadObservability through the shell's existing runtime subscription; the test observes one fake source, a fetch count 1->2 after revision 1, and a new count rendered. No second EventSource/subscription is added.

inventory.proofTestName: renders the success state from the real client

unproven: No real browser network/socket run; refresh is proved with the existing fake event source and injected fetch. The observability read is one route, not the whole wave.
